spec.goal: Make second and later rounds of build-implement's verify-fix loop structurally cheaper, without changing what a task that passes round 1 costs and without touching the Escalation contract. Evidence: across ten runs this venture has spent $41.15 against a $10 Brief budget and 13.8M tokens against 3M; build-implement is 72% of the dollars and 71% of the tokens; the three priciest runs are all fix loops (t2i alone was $4.38 and ended at max_rounds), four of eleven verified tasks failed their first panel, and the cheapest comparable run in the ledger is a verify_only re-panel at $0.36 against $1.22 for the same task's full round. Three changes in `.claude/workflows/build-implement.js`, each of which shortens a later round rather than the first. (1) Re-panel by finding resolution, not by verdict. Today `ctx.toRun = ctx.mode === 'all' ? LENSES : (failedLenses.length ? failedLenses : toRun)` is computed from which lenses returned `fail`, before the fixers and the Dispute Checker have run, so a lens whose every finding the judge OVERRULED is re-panelled anyway (and, when nothing was applied, `if (!applied.length) continue` re-panels exactly that lens on a byte-identical diff). The re-run set must instead be computed after the dispute rulings, from each finding's resolution: a lens re-runs only if it raised a finding that was fixed, upheld on dispute, deferred past the `MAX_FIXERS` cap, or otherwise left unresolved; a lens whose findings were all overruled is settled for this change set and joins `ctx.verified`, so the existing confirm pass — not a fresh retry round — is the only place it can run again. (2) Scope the fixer's input. A code fixer is given a location, evidence and a worktree, and pays a Sonnet-priced exploration of the whole tree to find the hunk it was told about. One cheap mechanical agent per failing round (label prefix `scope:`) slices the current cumulative diff at `ctx.changeSet.diff_ref` into one per-file patch per distinct finding file under `.artifacts/diffs/<task_id>.r<N>.scope.<n>.patch` and returns the file→path map; each code fixer's prompt then carries `scoped_diff_ref` and is told to read that slice first and widen only if it is insufficient. When a finding's location is not a file path, or slicing returns nothing, the fixer prompt falls back to today's unscoped wording, so the loop never blocks on the slicer. `.claude/agents/fixer.md` documents the new input and the read-the-slice-first rule; `.claude/agents/lens-spec-conformance.md` states that `location` must be a repository-relative path with a line number, because that string is now load-bearing for slicing, and that the lens may be re-panelled alone against an updated change set and must judge the whole diff, not only the fix. (3) Stop on cost, not only on round count. `ctx.tokens` is initialized to 0 and never incremented anywhere in the file, so `shouldEscalate`'s `ctx.tokens > TASK_TOKENS` branch is dead and `reason: "budget"` can never fire — a non-converging loop only ever stops at `K_ROUNDS`. Each round must measure its own spend as a `budget.spent()` delta, accumulate it into `ctx.tokens`, and compare against two ceilings: a per-task ceiling derived from the WorkItem budget the caller passes in the new optional `work_item_budgets` arg (`{ [work_item_id]: { tokens } }`, split evenly across that work item's tasks, falling back to `budget.task_tokens`, default 250000), and a per-round ceiling (`budget.round_tokens`, defaulting to task ceiling / `k_rounds`). A breach of either escalates with the existing enum value `budget`, checked before `max_rounds` so cost is the reported reason when cost is the cause, and the breach is recorded as one line in `ctx.history`. Because `pipeline` may overlap tasks and `budget.spent()` is a run-level counter, the delta is an upper bound on a task's spend; over-attribution only stops a failing loop sooner, which is the fail-safe direction, and it can never fire on a passing round because `shouldEscalate` is only reached after a non-pass. To make any of this testable, all seven decisions must be pure JavaScript in one extractable block delimited by the exact lines `// ---- BEGIN fix-loop decisions ----` and `// ---- END fix-loop decisions ----`, referencing no runtime handle (`args`, `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, `phase`, `log`, `budget`) and containing no `await`, so a test can read the workflow file, cut the block and evaluate it with `new Function`. Acceptance tests are Node's built-in runner and land in `substrate/test/`, so `/build-implement` must be invoked for this work item with `repo: "."` and `test_dir: "substrate/test"`.

Changing the integration barrier, the test-landing step, `tests_landed`/`tests_skipped`, the canary path, the `verify_only` path, or the topological task ordering.
Caching or reusing lens verdicts across runs, persisting fix-loop state between invocations, or any change to the ledger, Method Ledger or Company Memory schemas.
Moving any of the three stated venture success metrics — this is a budget and kill-criteria change, and the Roadmap Gate should weigh it as such.
risk_reasons: All new arguments are optional and additive; existing callers without `work_item_budgets` or `scoped_diff_ref` behave identically to today
Escalation contract is byte-identical including reason enum; new cost escalation uses existing `budget` value
No stored data shape changes; contracts.schema.json explicitly remains unchanged per AC-17
Fallback paths for all three changes ensure graceful degradation (slicing failure, missing scoped_diff, absent work_item_budgets)
All modifications are internal to build-implement workflow and lens agent documentation; no public routes or external consumer contracts affected
First-round panel behavior explicitly preserved per AC-14 so tasks passing round 1 cost exactly the same
Fully reversible algorithm changes with zero infrastructure or auth dependencies

tasks.description: Implement fix-loop cost optimization in build-implement workflow. (1) Extract decision functions (scopeOf, scopeTargets, nextLenses, lensesToRun, roundBudget, taskCeiling, shouldEscalate) into a pure-JavaScript block delimited by sentinel comments, recomputing toRun after dispute resolution based on finding resolutions rather than verdict verdicts, so lenses whose findings were all overruled do not re-panel. (2) Add a cheap mechanical agent (label prefix 'scope:') that slices the cumulative diff into per-file patches stored in `.artifacts/diffs/<task_id>.r<N>.scope.<n>.patch`, and pass scoped_diff_ref to fixers with a fallback to unscoped behavior. (3) Introduce per-task and per-round token budgets derived from a new optional work_item_budgets argument, track cumulative spend across rounds, and escalate on cost before max_rounds. Update fixer.md to document scoped_diff_ref input and the read-slice-first rule. Update lens-spec-conformance.md to state that location must be a repository-relative path with line numbers (for slicing) and that the lens may be re-panelled alone. Ensure all decision logic is testable by extracting it to pure functions with no runtime handles or await statements.

spec.goal: Make `ledger append` read a run's facts out of the runtime's own task output file instead of the operator's fingers, and make it refuse a wall clock it can prove is wrong. Today `substrate/ledger.js append` requires four hand-carried values (`--started`, `--result`, `--tokens-by-model`, `--agents`), and `substrate/lib/run-output.js` only prints two of them; the operator runs three commands and retypes a JSON object between them. That retyping already corrupted the ledger: run `m2-maintain-triage` carries `started_at 2026-09-11T03:36:00Z` against a real `finished_at` of `03:33:58.960Z`, and `ledger.js:46`'s `Math.max(0, Math.round((finished - started)/1000))` silently clamped the resulting -121s to `wall_clock_sec: 0` beside 338,559 real tokens, so every `summary --by method` row for `hotl` under-counts wall clock and mis-averages it. Three changes: (1) add `--from-output <task.output>`, which derives `agents`, `tokens_by_model`, `tokens`, the run `result` payload and BOTH timestamps from the output file's `workflowProgress` entries (`queuedAt`/`startedAt`/`lastProgressAt`/`durationMs`, epoch ms) and `doc.result`, demoting `--started`, `--result`, `--tokens`, `--tokens-by-model` and `--agents` to overrides; (2) drop the clamp — a `finished_at` before `started_at`, or a `wall_clock_sec` of 0 on a run with non-zero tokens, exits non-zero and writes nothing; (3) print the per-run cost and the per-model token/cost split on a successful append so no second command is needed. The one already-corrupt row is marked rather than guessed at: the true `started_at` is unrecoverable (the m2 trace and `.artifacts/maintain/m2/` are gone, `.artifacts` is not committed), so a new optional `wall_clock_unknown` flag on `LedgerEntry` keeps the row's real tokens in the Method Ledger while taking its fabricated wall clock out of the aggregate. Every existing flag, exit code and output line keeps working.

Back-computing or guessing a plausible `started_at` for `m2-maintain-triage`; the trace and `.artifacts/maintain/m2/` are gone and a fabricated timestamp is the exact failure this work item exists to stop.

Auto-discovering the task.output path (scanning the session task directory); the operator still passes it.
Batch or multi-file append, and any change to the one-row-per-run `ledger/index.jsonl` format beyond the new optional field.

Pre-existing test suite passes unmodified (AC-7 requirement), with no changes to existing assertions
Schema change is purely additive: LedgerEntry gains optional wall_clock_unknown field not in required list, existing rows validate without it (AC-11)
Stdout format changes are additive only: first line unchanged (AC-6), new per-model lines added for cost transparency
No auth, secrets, payments, or infrastructure touches
Single existing row modification (m2-maintain-triage) is a data correction via optional flag, fully reversible
New validation (refusing timestamp inversions) catches a known corruption pattern (AC-4 regression test), doesn't break valid workflows
No changes to /build-implement workflow's args, return shape, or escalation contract—this is a substrate tool change
All changes confined to substrate/ and substrate/test/; toy/ venture untouched
Output format additions (ledger summary wall_unknown_runs column, ledger list ?s rendering) are optional from reader perspective
